verdict.rationale: Discord's official REST API accepts either a bot token or an OAuth2 bearer token. The OAuth2 docs describe scope-gated access, for example a scope that allows /users/@me/connections. The Gateway delivers server events over WebSocket, and webhooks and the API post messages into channels, so an agent can be wired up through official, authenticated channels. Missing for 10: no explicit documentation of read-channel-messages endpoints or message-content access, no detail on fine-grained scopes or bot permissions for message read/write, no OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404), and no independent hands-on corroboration of agent use.
